course.title: Russian A1 · Pareto-first survival path
course.design: Prioritize a small high-leverage core, then expand breadth through repeated meaningful use.

paretoTiers.label: Survival core
paretoTiers.description: The smallest high-leverage set for introductions, repair, questions, needs, time, food, places, and basic navigation.
paretoTiers.targetBehavior: Prioritize in first exposure, daily sessions, adaptive review, and checkpoint recovery.

paretoTiers.label: High-frequency A1 core
paretoTiers.description: Common words and chunks that unlock most recurring beginner interactions after the survival layer.
paretoTiers.targetBehavior: Recycle across multiple units and modalities before adding supporting breadth.

paretoTiers.label: Supporting breadth
paretoTiers.description: Lower-frequency or contextual material that adds flexibility after the core is stable.
paretoTiers.targetBehavior: Introduce when core performance and learner capacity support it.

u03-numbers-time.title: Numbers, dates, and time
u03-numbers-time.objective: Ask and answer simple questions about numbers, days, dates, and the time of a meeting.

activities.title: Wake up the core
activities.prompt: Say today, tomorrow, and now before learning new numbers.

activities.title: Meet the time words
activities.prompt: Connect each Russian word to a useful beginner meaning.

activities.title: Listen for the number
activities.prompt: Hear the phrase, notice the stressed syllable, then repeat it aloud.

activities.title: Build a simple answer
activities.prompt: Answer «Который час?» with a time, then answer «Во сколько?» with в + time.

activities.title: Use it in a plan
activities.prompt: Complete the short dialogue and understand the tiny story.

patterns.en: What time is it? — It is three o’clock now.

patterns.ru: Во сколько встречаемся? — В три часа.
patterns.en: What time shall we meet? — At three o’clock.
patterns.pron: vo SKOL-ka fstre-CHA-yem-sya? — f tree cha-SA

grammar.title: Который час? vs Во сколько?
grammar.explanation: Use «Который час?» to ask the current time. Use «Во сколько?» to ask when an event happens. A simple answer uses «В» plus the time: «В три часа».
grammar.exampleRu: Во сколько встречаемся? — В три часа.
grammar.exampleEn: What time shall we meet? — At three o’clock.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not use the current-time question when you mean the time of an appointment.

turns.prompt: Say that it is three o’clock.
Say that you will meet at three.

lines.en: Tomorrow I work in the morning.

checkpoint.title: Quick time check

questions.prompt: Choose the natural answer to «Во сколько?».
Choose the phrase for “What time is it?”.

checkpoint.completionRule: Answer at least 2 of 3 correctly and complete both dialogue turns.

u02-greetings-introductions.title: Greetings and introductions
u02-greetings-introductions.objective: Greet someone, exchange names, and say where you are from in a short Russian conversation.

activities.title: Open the conversation
activities.prompt: Choose a greeting that fits the situation.

activities.title: Build your introduction
activities.prompt: Connect names and origins to useful meanings.

activities.title: Notice the question
activities.prompt: Hear the difference between informal and formal name questions.

activities.title: Say who you are
activities.prompt: Answer «Как тебя зовут?» with your name.

activities.title: Meet someone new
activities.prompt: Complete the dialogue and follow the short story.

patterns.en: Where are you from? — I am from Canada.

grammar.title: Ты vs Вы
grammar.explanation: Use «ты» with friends and people your age when the situation is informal. Use «вы» for a stranger, an older person, or a polite interaction. «Как вас зовут?» is the safe formal question.
grammar.exampleRu: Как вас зовут? — Меня зовут Анна.
grammar.exampleEn: What is your name? — My name is Anna.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not switch to «ты» with a stranger before the situation becomes informal.

lines.en: This is my new friend Mark.

checkpoint.title: First meeting check

questions.prompt: Choose the natural answer to «Как тебя зовут?»
Choose the phrase for “I am from Moscow”.

checkpoint.completionRule: Answer at least 2 of 3 correctly and complete both dialogue turns.

u04-people-family.title: People and family
u04-people-family.objective: Describe the important people around you and ask who someone is using simple Russian sentences.

activities.title: Name the people
activities.prompt: Retrieve the family and friend words you need most.

activities.title: Meet the people
activities.prompt: Connect people words to their meanings and genders.

activities.title: Hear who it is
activities.prompt: Notice the difference between «он» and «она».

activities.title: Describe your family
activities.prompt: Build a sentence with мой, моя, он, or она.

activities.title: Introduce someone
activities.prompt: Complete the dialogue and understand the family story.

patterns.en: Who is this? — This is my brother.

patterns.ru: Он мой друг. Она моя подруга.
patterns.en: He is my friend. She is my friend.
patterns.pron: on moy drook. a-NA ma-YA pa-DOO-ga

grammar.title: Мой or моя? Он or она?
grammar.explanation: Use «мой» with a masculine noun such as брат or друг, and «моя» with a feminine noun such as сестра or подруга. Use «он» for he and «она» for she.
grammar.exampleRu: Это моя сестра. Она моя подруга.
grammar.exampleEn: This is my sister. She is my friend.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not use «мой» before a feminine noun: say «моя сестра».

turns.prompt: Say that this is your sister.
Say that this is your brother.

lines.en: And this is my sister Nina.

checkpoint.title: People check

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrase for “my sister”.
Choose the phrase for “Who is this?”.
Choose the correct pronoun for Нина.

checkpoint.completionRule: Answer at least 2 of 3 correctly and complete both dialogue turns.

u05-home-objects.title: Home and everyday objects
u05-home-objects.objective: Talk about what is at home while reusing greetings, family, time, and meeting phrases in one connected beginner conversation.

activities.title: Return to the core
activities.prompt: Bring greetings, family words, and time phrases back before adding home words.

activities.title: Name the home
activities.prompt: Connect the most useful home and object words to their meanings.

activities.title: Hear the contrast
activities.prompt: Listen for who, when, and where in short recycled questions.

activities.title: Build a home sentence
activities.prompt: Say what is at home and when someone will meet you.

activities.title: Host a simple visit
activities.prompt: Complete the recycled dialogue, story, and cumulative checkpoint.

patterns.en: The book is on the table.

grammar.title: Где? — дома, здесь, там
grammar.explanation: Use «дома» for being at home, «здесь» for here, and «там» for there. The phrase «в три часа» keeps the appointment pattern from Unit 3 active.
grammar.exampleRu: Сегодня мы дома. Приходи в три часа.
grammar.exampleEn: Today we are at home. Come over at three o’clock.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not answer «Где?» with «дом» when you mean location; use «дома».

turns.prompt: Say that you are at home.
Invite your friend for three o’clock.

lines.en: Hello! Today we are at home.
The book is on the table.
Mark is coming at three o’clock.
In the evening we are together.

recycling.title: Cumulative listening loop
recycling.summary: This unit deliberately brings back high-value phrases from Units 2, 3, and 4 before adding home vocabulary. Hear the question, identify the contrast, then reuse the answer in the story.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Здравствуйте!» — what kind of phrase is it?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This returns the formal greeting from Unit 2.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «В три часа» — what does it answer?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This returns the appointment answer from Unit 3.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Моя сестра» — who is being described?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This returns feminine agreement from Unit 4.

checkpoint.title: Cumulative home visit check

questions.prompt: Choose the natural answer to «Где ты?»
Choose the answer to «Во сколько приходить?»
Choose the correct phrase for “my sister”.
Choose the formal greeting for a visitor.

checkpoint.completionRule: Answer at least 3 of 4 correctly and complete both dialogue turns.
